name: Red-Neon Serif / 80s Synth-Horror
summary: 80s synth-horror title card: a high-contrast serif wordmark burning in red neon on near-black #050505, off-white mono copy, faint film grain and a heavy vignette.
whenToUse: When the user asks for a Stranger Things-style title treatment, red-neon serif wordmark, 80s synth-horror poster, VHS title card, or a dark cinematic landing page with a single glowing headline.

effects.grain: repeating-radial-gradient(circle at 17% 32%, rgba(232, 226, 216, 0.035) 0 1px, transparent 1px 3px), repeating-radial-gradient(circle at 71% 68%, rgba(255, 26, 26, 0.03) 0 1px, transparent 1px 4px)

rules: Red is light, not fill: #ff1a1a appears only as glow, glyph, 1px rule, or mark on near-black — never as a large plate behind text and never on more than one primary action per screen.

Layer the bloom: every neon element carries a tight core plus wide falloff (0 0 1px #ff6f61, 0 0 8px rgba(255,26,26,.9), 0 0 28px rgba(255,26,26,.6), 0 0 64px rgba(179,0,0,.45)); a single blurred drop shadow reads as a smudge, not neon.

Scale type cinematically: display serif at 40px+ with line-height 0.95–1.05 and 0.02–0.08em tracking, IBM Plex Mono at 15–17px/1.6 for every paragraph, label, and value — the serif never sets running text below 24px.
Keep the ground near-black: surfaces live between #050505 and #1a0f0f and are separated by a 1px rgba(179,0,0,.45) hairline or a bloom — never by a lighter gray card or a white border.
Use off-white #e8e2d8 for type and #ffffff only for a 1px specular highlight; de-emphasize with #8a7f76 rather than opacity, so the grain layer never washes text out.
Texture is film, not noise: grain at 3–5% opacity and a 30%→black vignette sit above the background and below content with pointer-events: none, and switch off for print and reduced-motion.
Move slowly and analog: 240ms color fades, 600ms panel reveals, 2400ms glow pulses on cubic-bezier(0.22,0.61,0.36,1); the wordmark flicker is the only stutter and only when motion is allowed.
One glow per view: the wordmark or the single primary action owns the bloom, and everything else stays flat deep red #b30000 so the hierarchy never collapses into a red blur.

componentRecipes.panel: background: #120b0b; color: #e8e2d8; border: 1px solid rgba(179, 0, 0, 0.45); border-radius: 2px; padding: 24px 32px; box-shadow: 0 24px 60px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.75), 0 0 40px rgba(255, 26, 26, 0.06); — the red hairline plus the deep ambient drop is the entire container. Optional grain layer from effects.grain at 4% opacity, positioned above the panel background and below its content, pointer-events: none. No backdrop-blur, no white border, no large red fill, no radius above 2px.
componentRecipes.wordmark: The signature: font: 700 clamp(48px, 9vw, 120px)/0.95 'Cinzel', 'Playfair Display', 'Cormorant Garamond', Georgia, serif; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: #ff1a1a; background: #050505; text-shadow: 0 0 1px #ff6f61, 0 0 8px rgba(255, 26, 26, 0.9), 0 0 28px rgba(255, 26, 26, 0.6), 0 0 64px rgba(179, 0, 0, 0.45); — sit it in the upper third with 32–56px beneath and a caption line in 13px #8a7f76 Plex Mono. The flicker keyframe dips opacity to 0.92 twice per 2400ms cycle, never below 0.9, and is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
componentRecipes.button: font: 600 14px/1 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.14em; background: transparent; color: #ff1a1a; border: 1px solid #b30000; border-radius: 2px; padding: 14px 24px; text-shadow: 0 0 6px rgba(255, 26, 26, 0.55); transition: color 240ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1), border-color 240ms, box-shadow 240ms; :hover { color: #ff6f61; border-color: #ff1a1a; box-shadow: 0 0 12px rgba(255, 26, 26, 0.45), inset 0 0 18px rgba(255, 26, 26, 0.12); } :active { transform: translateY(1px); box-shadow: inset 0 0 24px rgba(255, 26, 26, 0.3); } :focus-visible { outline: 1px solid #e8e2d8; outline-offset: 3px; } — primary variant: background #b30000, color #e8e2d8, box-shadow 0 0 24px rgba(255, 26, 26, 0.4); it is the only element allowed a red fill, and only once per screen.
componentRecipes.input: background: #050505; color: #e8e2d8; font: 16px/1.6 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; border: 1px solid rgba(179, 0, 0, 0.5); border-bottom-color: #b30000; border-radius: 2px; padding: 12px 16px; caret-color: #ff1a1a; box-shadow: inset 0 0 24px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9); :placeholder { color: #8a7f76; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em; font-size: 13px; } :focus { border-color: #ff1a1a; box-shadow: inset 0 0 24px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9), 0 0 16px rgba(255, 26, 26, 0.3); outline: none; } — invalid state: border-color #ff4a3d plus a Plex Mono message prefixed 'SIGNAL FAULT' below; a red border alone is never the error signal.
componentRecipes.statusbar: height: 44px; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 32px; padding: 0 24px; background: #050505; border-top: 1px solid rgba(179, 0, 0, 0.45); font: 12px/1 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.16em; color: #8a7f76; live value in #e8e2d8, alert in #ff1a1a with 0 0 10px rgba(255, 26, 26, 0.5); segments split by 1px rgba(232, 226, 216, 0.12) rules; the live indicator is a 6px #ff1a1a dot pulsing at 2400ms and it always carries the word LIVE beside it.
componentRecipes.menu: A vertical rail of links, no bullets: item { display: block; font: 13px/1 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.14em; padding: 12px 16px; color: #8a7f76; border-radius: 2px; } selected item turns #e8e2d8 with a 2px #ff1a1a left rule and a 0 0 12px rgba(255, 26, 26, 0.35) bloom on the rule only; hover fades to #e8e2d8 over 240ms; group separators are a 1px rgba(179, 0, 0, 0.35) rule with 24px margin — never a filled red bar.

copywriting.voice: Late-night small-town radio: hushed, present tense, second person, a little ominous. The interface speaks like a transmission that knows more than it says — short declarative lines, one idea per sentence, and no jokes.
avoid: series character, place, or brand names
cutesy or apologetic loading copy ('Oops', 'just a moment')
pure white body text and neon-red paragraphs

do: Put the red on black: hold every surface between #050505 and #1a0f0f and let #ff1a1a exist only as glow, glyph, or a 1px mark.
Set the wordmark in the display serif at 48px or larger, uppercase, with the four-stop red bloom and 32–56px of dark breathing room beneath it.
Set every paragraph, label, and value in IBM Plex Mono at 15–17px, and reserve the serif for display lines at 24px and up.
Separate surfaces with a 1px deep-red hairline plus a deep ambient drop shadow, and keep radius at 0–2px so panels read as film frames.
Animate slowly and once: 240ms color fades, 600ms reveals, 2400ms glow pulses, and a single 0.92-opacity flicker on the wordmark.
Cap film grain at 4–5% opacity and a 30%-to-black vignette, layered over the background and under all content with pointer-events: none.
Pair every glowing signal with a word — LIVE, WARNING, SIGNAL LOST — so state never rides on red alone.
dont: Don't fill large areas with #ff1a1a or #b30000 — red is light, not a background, and one filled primary button per screen is the ceiling.
Don't blur depth: no soft gray drop shadows, no backdrop-blur, no glassmorphism cards — depth is a red bloom or a 1px hairline.
Don't set body copy in the display serif, don't take the serif below 24px, and don't apply the bloom to paragraphs.
Don't use #ffffff for text or fade text with opacity — muted copy is #8a7f76, never rgba(232,226,216,.5).
Don't add bouncy, springy, spinning, or parallax motion; nothing should feel like a modern app landing page.
Don't reproduce series logos, character or place names, or episode artwork — evoke the treatment, not the assets.
Don't round into pills, add 12px radii, or stack more than one glow in the same viewport.
accessibility: Body copy #e8e2d8 on #050505 clears 4.5:1 by a wide margin and muted #8a7f76 lands near 5:1; #ff1a1a on #050505 is roughly 5.2:1 raw, but bloom and grain eat into that, so keep red text runs short and push the glow to display sizes.
Honor prefers-reduced-motion: stop the wordmark flicker and glow pulses, freeze the scanline and grain overlays, and leave the emblem at full opacity — still red, just steady.
Keep grain, vignette, and haze off the text layer and off focus rings: max 5% opacity, pointer-events: none, and disabled under forced-colors and print.
Never encode state by red alone — pair it with LIVE / WARNING / SIGNAL LOST labels, and keep a 1px #e8e2d8 outline at 3px offset on every focusable element, never on a flickering element.
signatureElement: The red-neon serif wordmark: a high-contrast display serif in #ff1a1a with a four-stop red bloom on near-black #050505, under faint film grain and a heavy vignette

prose.overview: This mode is the title card before the show: a near-black #050505 field, a high-contrast serif wordmark burning in red, and a faint film grain over everything. It dresses an interface in 80s synth-horror — hushed, analog, lit from inside the letters — instead of in chrome or pixel hardware. The result should feel like a transmission arriving at night: calm layout, one glowing line, and a great deal of dark around it.
prose.colors: The field is #050505 with surfaces one step up at #120b0b and never lighter than #1a0f0f; body text is off-white #e8e2d8 and the single muted tone is #8a7f76. Red carries the light: #b30000 is the structural red used for hairlines, borders, and flat marks, while #ff1a1a is the emitted red reserved for the wordmark, the one primary action, and live signal. Warm accents — amber #e0a83a, muted green #6fbf8b, alert coral #ff4a3d — appear only in status chrome and never as surfaces. The variants preserve that hierarchy: title lists the wordmark ramp, upsideDown darkens toward #7a0c0c and ash, and synthNight adds magenta and teal for a rare secondary glow that never covers more than a sliver of the page.
prose.typography: Display type is a high-contrast serif — Cinzel or Playfair Display for the uppercase wordmark and hero headings, Cormorant Garamond when a lighter editorial line is wanted — always 40px and up, line-height 0.95–1.05, tracked 0.02–0.08em. IBM Plex Mono carries everything else: paragraphs at 15–17px/1.6, labels and buttons at 12–14px uppercase with 0.14em tracking, values in tabular figures with a red caret. The serif is never asked to set running text and the mono never carries the hero, so the contrast between burning letterform and quiet machine text stays absolute. Georgia and serif, then Courier New and monospace, are honest fallbacks — no fake italic, weight, or glow is used to invent hierarchy the type cannot hold.
prose.layout: Layout is widescreen and central: a narrow measure of 60–72 mono characters, generous 32–56px breathing room, and one dominant wordmark or headline in the upper third of the view. Content is anchored to a 4/8/16/32/56 spacing scale and centred in a max-width column, with a persistent 44px signal strip along the bottom. Panels are film frames rather than cards — full-width dark rectangles with a 1px red hairline — so the layout reads as a frame around the glow instead of a stack of floating boxes. Nothing is crowded: a second focal point, if the screen truly needs one, is a mid-size serif subtitle, not another bloom.
prose.elevation: Depth is ambient darkness plus emitted light: a panel sits on the field behind a 1px rgba(179,0,0,.45) hairline and a deep 0 24px 60px rgba(0,0,0,.75) drop, while glowing elements add a layered bloom with a tight #ff6f61 core, an 8px #ff1a1a mid, and 28px and 64px falloff. Nothing floats with glass or backdrop-blur; separation comes from the hairline and the black gap. The glow scale is fixed — 0 0 12px interactive, 0 0 28px wordmark, 0 0 64px hero — so two elements never compete at the same intensity. The only hard offset in the system is the 6px 6px 0 #000000 used for a rare detached dialog.
prose.shapes: Shapes stay rectilinear and nearly sharp: radius 2px on panels, buttons, and inputs so edges read as film-frame corners rather than app pills, with hairline weights of exactly 1px. Rules and dividers are 1px deep-red or 12%-opacity off-white lines, never 2px bars or filled red bands. Icons are thin 1.5px strokes in #e8e2d8 or #b30000, and the glow is the only soft geometry allowed — it is light, so it may fall off. Nothing is rounded past 2px, and the sole circle in the system is the 6px live-signal dot.
prose.components: Panels are #120b0b frames with a 1px red hairline, 24–32px padding, and a deep ambient drop, optionally under a 4% grain layer. The wordmark is the hero: uppercase serif at clamp(48px, 9vw, 120px) in #ff1a1a with a four-stop bloom and quiet mono copy beneath it. Buttons are 1px #b30000 outlined mono labels that brighten to #ff6f61 and gain a 12px bloom on hover, while the single filled variant — #b30000 with #e8e2d8 text and a 24px glow — is allowed once per screen. Inputs are black wells with a #b30000 bottom rule, a red caret, and a 'SIGNAL FAULT' message on error, and the status bar is a 44px strip of tracked uppercase mono whose pulsing dot always carries the word LIVE.
prose.dosDonts: Do keep the ground at #050505 and let red only glow, do set the wordmark large and all paragraphs in IBM Plex Mono, do layer a tight core with a wide bloom instead of one blurred shadow, and do animate slowly — 240ms fades, 2400ms pulses, one flicker. Don't fill surfaces with red, don't add pill radii or glassmorphism, don't glow body text, don't lift the ground toward gray, and don't borrow the series' logos, names, or artwork — this mode evokes the treatment and reproduces none of it.
